_why: The shipped adapter's measured recall band. Nothing else in the suite fails if a pipeline change silently moves this number, and one has: the 2026-10-28 merge fix lifted every baseline by ~.025 and was only noticed because someone re-ran the baselines by hand. Re-scoring these stored runs is deterministic -- the model does not run again -- so any drift here is a change in the scoring or filtering code, which is exactly what this pins.
_fingerprint_note: code_fingerprint identifies the code that PRODUCED the runs, recorded in each run's pipeline_config.json and carried into the replay report. Re-scoring under new code keeps it unchanged, so it pins the inputs, not the scorer. The recall band is what pins the scorer.
_tolerance_note: Replay is deterministic given stored predictions, so the expected drift is zero; .0005 is an eighth of the .0040 band width and a twenty-eighth of the .0140 baseline seed spread -- wide enough for float and ordering noise, far too narrow to admit a real scoring change.
